q: Our paediatrician recommended doing cry it out because we have been having such a problem with his sleep.

q: His doctor thinks he’s too old and we left it too long. Then in my mommy group I see people talking about how well their kids nap and I feel like a failure as a mother.

q: my husband isn’t proactive in baby things and generally just follows my lead unless he thinks I’m being ridiculous from the onset.
x: Same mother on who drives the sleep decisions.

q: I should try the extension of windows and letting him try to fall asleep. I think I’m scared of the level of crying I will encounter.
x: Same mother replying to commenters.

q: Every time we work out a method to get him to go back to sleep without our intervention it only works for a couple of weeks.
x: Working mother of a 2.5-year-old with three months of night crying and bedtime fear.

x: Breastfeeding mother of an almost 10-month-old, now asking about two night feeds.

q: She was 3/3.5/4 and it was too much awake time at bedtime so switched it to 3.15/3.5/3.5-3.75 for almost a week now & its going better had multiple wakes at night & now down to 2 with the new awake times

q: Tried modified Ferber around 7 months and that extended our first stretch to 3 hours,  peaking at 5 hours by night 5. Then we had 4 teeth come in and travel, which totally derailed us.
x: Breastfeeding mother of a 9-month-old who has 'always been an awful sleeper'.

q: I‘ve felt like a huge failure as a mom, because there’s only one thing I can do to comfort him.
x: Same mother: neither parent can calm him by picking up.

q: Last week we got our schedule back to 3/3.5/4 and tried to re-Ferberize. The last 4 nights have been truly awful because he learned to stand in his crib.
x: Same mother on the restart; after 40 minutes her husband switched to full crying it out.

q: Has anyone had any luck starting with a gradual method to get sensitive cosleeping babies used to the crib? Or am I just wasting my time/sanity by not truly going all-in on CIO and comforting him during these night wakes?
x: Same mother; she thinks her 'very determined heavy screamer' could cry all night.

q: Thank you, I’ve cleared the rest of this week so we can stay disciplined to 7:30 wakes and will try bumping our first wake window to 3.5 for more awake time.
x: Same mother after a commenter's schedule advice.

q: At his 9-month checkup, our pediatrician shrugged and said that because he gets so much night sleep, naps are "just going to be a struggle" for him.
x: Nursing mother of a nearly 10-month-old who sleeps 11–12 hours but will not nap in the crib.

q: I am admittedly unclear on how CIO works with naps, specifically how long to leave them crying, but I try for 20-30 minutes before intervening and offering another option. Doing that twice a day is very taxing and affects his bedtime
x: Same mother; gradual crying it out fixed nights but not naps.

q: However, as good of a night sleeper as he is (I chalk that up entirely to temperament and luck, and I definitely do not take it for granted), he has always struggled with his naps.
x: Same mother; former smart-bassinet users until 6 months.

x: Mother of a 12-month-old who needs to be held to fall asleep.

q: I don't mind helping her fall alseep at night, but naps are becoming heavy and exhausting. She also starts daycare soon which worries me.
x: Same mother; she holds the baby another 45–90 minutes to extend each nap.

q: So then i try to sleep train, but it always ends up with her extremely upset and full of puke.
x: Same mother on the cycle of trying and stopping.

q: I was really happy, first time having a no milk night and she fell asleep a few times on her own because she was too tired to sit up (which usually means she can cry for a very very long time). I am hopeful with the schedule change we will continue making positive baby steps.
x: Same mother the next night, after a commenter suggested a fixed schedule.

x: Mother of a 17-month-old trained with Ferber at 13 months; molars arrived at 15 months.

q: It feels like we went 2 steps forward, 5 steps back. Why is it not sticking this time around? Any advice?
x: Same mother on night 5 of the retrain.

x: Same mother: the retrain used the old schedule unchanged; a commenter suggested a longer last window.

q: So today his nap was only 45 minutes. Do I still keep a 6.5 hr wake window for the afternoon?
x: Same mother the next day, back to the commenter with the next decision.

x: First-time working parent of a formula-fed 5.5-month-old who wakes twice to eat and resettles easily.

q: Of course a full night sleep would be great but I’m mostly adjusted to this routine of his and I like the few extra minutes I get with him since I work during the week and feel like I don’t see him enough.
